key_insight: AI-derived ECG features outperformed selected morphology measurements for 30-day mortality prediction but showed no clear discrimination gain over expanded automated ECG reports when basic clinical history was included.
clinical_relevance: Similar overall performance can conceal different patient prioritization: AI-feature and report-based models captured nearly identical numbers of deaths while sharing only about half of flagged patients.
method: Compared pretrained AI-derived ECG features with 15 prespecified ECG morphology measurements using identical prediction-model procedures.
Held age, recorded sex, and prior-diagnosis indicators constant in adjusted comparisons; assessed paired 95% confidence intervals.
Examined hypothetical 5% review lists and post hoc comparisons with expanded automated ECG reports.
evidence_signal: Among 25,430 held-out MIMIC-IV patients with 924 deaths, AI features improved AUROC over morphology by 0.075 (95% CI 0.059–0.091), but adding AI to reports plus clinical history yielded 0.0075 (−0.0005–0.0151).
watch_item: Report-based and review-list comparisons were post hoc, and hypothetical prioritization does not establish improved clinical outcomes.
paper_title: Evaluating the Incremental Value of AI-Derived ECG Features Beyond Automated ECG Reports and Clinical Data for 30-Day Mortality: A MIMIC-IV Cohort Study
